agent.problem: Too many choices require discovery or luck rather than reasoning from the earlier cards. Cards 5, 7, 10, 14 and 15 ask for the offering types, garment material, number of goats, method of choosing between them and scapegoat's fate without providing any way to reason those details out. That is five of the stop's ten choices, leaving at most half as informed guesses rather than most.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

agent.problem: The stop again relies too heavily on uninformed discovery. At most four of the eight choices are informed guesses, so this stretch becomes a guessing game.

agent.problem: Choice cards 10, 11 and 13 depend on "This day" or "this day" without identifying which day they mean. The date was introduced back on story card 8, which is no longer on screen. Each question should carry enough context itself, such as identifying the day of atonement or the tenth day of the seventh month.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
